the three 6-fluoroethyl-orvinols are suitable as functional analogues of their native C-11 labeled versions and that [(18)F]-fluoroethyl-diphrenorphine, a new 6-O-(1(18)F)fluoroethylated opioid antagonist, was prepared and tested in vivo in rats.

the three 6-0-[18F]fluoroalkylated derivatives of diprenorphine (antagonist), buprenorphines (partial agonist), and orvinol (full agonist) have similar pharmacological profiles to their native carbon-11 analogues, and are suitable candidates as PET radioligands to study opioid receptor systems in vivo in humans.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel series of 6-O-[18]fluoroethylated derivatives, with different intrinsic activities, of structurally related 6-oxo-orphanin FQ analogues, which are potential ligands of the ORL1 receptor.
the synthesis of 6-O-[(18)F] fluoromethylated orvinols, which can be considered as potential radiotracers for the in vivo study of the μ opioid receptor.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
[(18)F]-labeled 6-O-(2-fluoroethyl)-orvinols can serve as suitable functional analogues of their native C-11 counterparts and can be used as radioligands for the study of mu-opioid receptors.

the 6-O-(fluoroethyl) substitution is an appropriate and useful approach for radiolabeling of the three structurally related orvionols with [(18)F], and that [(18)F]-labeled orvinols are useful for imaging of opioid receptor systems with PET.
the three [(18)F]-6-O-(fluoroethyl)-orvinol derivatives are suitable candidates to be used in vivo in PET imaging studies to investigate the pharmacology of opioid receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
[(18)F]-labeled orvinols can be used as functional analogues for [(11)C]-labeled orvinoles for the in vivo study of the mu-opioid receptor system in humans and other species.

the three 6-(18)F-labeled orvinal derivatives are suitable candidates as PET tracers for opioid receptor imaging.
